case_name: Jatin Narendrabhai Sanghvi & Ors v State of Gujarat & Anr
citation: R/Criminal Misc. Application No. 18659 of 2023 (Gujarat HC, 19 June 2026) -- no independent neutral/SCC citation confirmed
text:
11.      So far as Sections 66C and 66D of the Information
                       Technology Act, 2000 are concerned, Section 66C relates to
                       identity theft, whereas Section 66D deals with cheating by
                       personation through the use of a computer resource. Upon
                       perusal of the FIR and the charge-sheet papers, no material is
                       found to suggest that the petitioners forged or dishonestly
                       used the electronic identity of any other person. There is also
                       no material to show that the petitioners created any fake
                       profile, gained unauthorized access to any account, or cheated
                       any person by impersonation through a computer resource.

12.      Not an iota of oral or documentary evidence has been
                       placed on record to demonstrate how the petitioners cheated
                       any person or impersonated another individual for the
                       purpose of cheating. Mere use of a mobile phone, in the
                       absence of such material, would not attract the provisions of
                       Sections 66C or 66D of the Information Technology Act, 2000.
